  selection_verb:

references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/videos/who-where-how-apt-attacks-q2-2025-q3-2025/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/update-winrar-tools-now-romcom-and-others-exploiting-zero-day-vulnerability/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-8088

  - attack.t1203

    TargetFilename|contains: '\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_path
falsepositives:

level: high

3756.def:
// CVE-2025-8088 / RomCom — archive utility silently writes a persistence artefact
// into the per-user Startup folder during what looks like a routine extraction.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip32.exe","winzip64.exe","wzzip.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where FileName endswith ".lnk"
      or FileName endswith ".dll"
      or FileName endswith ".exe"
      or FileName endswith ".bat"
      or FileName endswith ".cmd"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Archiver = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ArchiverCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          DroppedFile = FileName,
          DroppedPath = FolderPath,
          SHA256, MD5, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
3756.sent:
// CVE-2025-8088 / RomCom — same intent on Sentinel via ASIM ImFileEvent
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip32.exe","winzip64.exe","wzzip.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".lnk"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".exe"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".bat"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".cmd"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Archiver = ActingProcessName,
          ArchiverCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          DroppedFile = TargetFileName,
          DroppedPath = TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc

  - attack.t1204.002

  category: file_event
  product: windows

    Image|endswith:
      - '\winrar.exe'
      - '\rar.exe'
      - '\unrar.exe'
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\7zg.exe'
      - '\7zfm.exe'
      - '\winzip32.exe'

3757.def:
// RomCom CVE-2025-8088 stage-2 — signed Python launched from a transient path so the
// adversary's adjacent malicious python3xx.dll satisfies the import search order.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "python.exe"
      or FileName =~ "pythonw.exe"
      or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^python3\d{1,2}\.exe$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
// suppress the rare legit case of a Python installer extracting itself
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          PythonImage = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
          ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
3757.sent:
// RomCom CVE-2025-8088 stage-2 on Sentinel ASIM (cross-vendor) — Python from a transient path.
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\python(w)?(3\d{0,2})?\.exe$"
| where TargetProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "msiexec.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

let lookback = 7d;
let htmlAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where FileType in~ ("html","htm") or FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm";
let unpkgUrls = EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where Url has "unpkg.com"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)unpkg\.com/(redirect-[a-z0-9]{6}|mad-[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+){5,})(@|/)"
        or Url has_any ("/beamglea.js","beamglea");
htmlAttachments
| join kind=inner unpkgUrls on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, FileType, SHA256, Url, UrlDomain

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RecordType in (28, 2)
| where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive","Create")
| where tostring(ItemAttachments) has_any (".html",".htm")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Parameters))), Sender = tostring(UserId), Recipients = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Parameters))), ItemAttachments, ClientIP

| where match(file_name, "(?i)\.html?$")

3803.sent:
// Hunt CVE-2025-29927 exploitation: external clients sending the bypass header to self-hosted Next.js apps.
// Header lives in WAF / reverse-proxy event text. AppServiceHTTPLogs does not surface arbitrary request
// headers, so we cover WAF (CommonSecurityLog) + raw nginx/IIS via Syslog/W3CIISLog where ingested.
let Window = 7d;
// Path 1 — WAF / reverse-proxy events that log full request headers/context
let WafHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where (RequestContext has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (Message has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString1 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString2 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString3 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString4 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString5 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString6 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct,
              DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication,
              Evidence = coalesce(RequestContext, Message, DeviceCustomString1, DeviceCustomString2, DeviceCustomString3, DeviceCustomString4, DeviceCustomString5, DeviceCustomString6),
              Layer = "WAF";
// Path 2 — raw nginx / Apache access logs forwarded via Syslog (some teams strip headers, some don't)
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where SyslogMessage has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = HostIP, SourceUserName = "", DeviceVendor = "linux", DeviceProduct = Facility,
              DestinationHostName = HostName, RequestURL = "", RequestMethod = "", RequestClientApplication = "",
              Evidence = SyslogMessage, Layer = "Syslog";
// Path 3 — IIS reverse-proxy in front of Next.js (header value sometimes ends up in csUriQuery via URL Rewrite Module)
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where csUriQuery has "x-middleware-subrequest" or csReferer has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, SourceUserName = csUserName, DeviceVendor = "iis", DeviceProduct = "W3CIISLog",
              DestinationHostName = Computer, RequestURL = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), RequestMethod = csMethod,
              RequestClientApplication = csUserAgent,
              Evidence = strcat(csUriQuery, " | ", csReferer), Layer = "IIS";
union isfuzzy=true WafHits, SyslogHits, IISHits
| extend SourceIP = tostring(SourceIP)
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleEvidence = any(Evidence), Hosts = make_set(DestinationHostName, 25),
            URLs = make_set(RequestURL, 25), UAs = make_set(RequestClientApplication, 10),
            Layers = make_set(Layer, 5)
    by SourceIP
| order by FirstSeen asc

// Memory dump primitive: python reading /proc/PID/mem (and usually /proc/PID/maps first)
let PythonProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName matches regex @"^python[23]?$"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker","/proc/","memdump.py","isSecret")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId=tostring(ProcessId), ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let MemReads = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName in~ ("mem","maps")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python[23]?$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessId=tostring(InitiatingProcessId), InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
MemReads
| join kind=inner (PythonProcs) on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine1
| order by Timestamp desc

let WindowMin = 10m;
let RestartThreshold = 3;   // empirical: legit reload is 1-2 spawns; a flood-induced crash loop spikes to >=3 inside 10 min
let HTTP2Servers = dynamic(["httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","node","node.exe","java","java.exe","envoy","envoy.exe","traffic_server","traffic_manager"]);
let Exposed = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where IsInternetFacing == true;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where FileName in~ (HTTP2Servers)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalina", "org.apache.catalina", "tomcat", "trafficserver")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
   and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("apt", "apt-get", "yum", "dnf", "rpm", "dpkg", "systemctl", "service", "docker", "containerd-shim", "podman", "kubelet", "ansible", "chef-client", "puppet", "saltstack")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "reload" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "graceful" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--test"
| summarize Restarts = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where Restarts >= RestartThreshold
| extend SpanSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| join kind=inner Exposed on DeviceId
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, SpanSec, Restarts, DeviceName, PublicIP, FileName, Parents, SampleCmd
| order by Restarts desc

3864.sigma:
title: sshd Loads Backdoored liblzma 5.6.0 / 5.6.1 (CVE-2024-3094)
id: 8b3c1a4e-7d2f-4f9a-9a2c-2b1f5d3c1a4e
status: experimental
description: Detects the OpenSSH daemon loading the malicious liblzma.so.5.6.0 or liblzma.so.5.6.1 introduced by the xz-utils supply chain backdoor (CVE-2024-3094). The backdoor activates when sshd, via libsystemd notification patches, chain-loads the compromised liblzma — at which point the IFUNC crc64_resolve audit hook hijacks RSA_public_decrypt and enables authentication bypass for a holder of the attacker's RSA key.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/the-xz-backdoor-cve-2024-3094/
  - https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2024-3094-detecting-the-sshd-backdoor-in-xz-utils
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3094
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/04/01
tags:
  - attack.t1574.006
  - attack.t1554
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sshd'
      - '/systemd'
  selection_lib:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.0'
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.1'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_lib
falsepositives:
  - Security research / IR lab hosts intentionally running the backdoored library
  - Snapshot of an older filesystem mounted for forensic review
level: critical

title: macOS Keyboard Text Replacements Dumped via defaults
id: 7d3a0f6e-1c5a-4e91-9c2c-1f3b8c2b5f10
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the macOS `defaults` CLI reading NSUserDictionaryReplacementItems, the global preference holding keyboard text replacements. Developers commonly bind sensitive snippets (passwords, SSH keys, credit-card numbers) to these macros, and the read can be triggered by any non-privileged process — including a malicious npm postinstall hook.
references:
    - https://snyk.io/blog/using-insecure-npm-package-manager-defaults/
    - https://www.yagiz.co/using-insecure-npm-defaults/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23

    - attack.credential_access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos

    selection_img:
        Image|endswith: '/defaults'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains: 'NSUserDictionaryReplacementItems'
    condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
